title: guard language_from_path hardcodes rust/dart — import_pattern lessons dead for Python/TS/JS/C

acceptance_criteria.text: language_from_path derives from default_registry() extension mapping, not a literal
Guard-level test: writing a new .py file with a matching import_pattern anchor surfaces the lesson
Constraint/pattern paths sharing parse_proposed reviewed for behavior change from the widened language set

root_cause:
`language_from_path` was written when the guard only needed Rust and Dart, and nothing forced it to track adapter registration. Because `parse_proposed` returns Option and `None` is indistinguishable from "parsed but no imports", the failure was silent: for a .py or .ts file the guard produced an empty import list and every import_pattern anchor simply failed to match. The absence of a signal — not a wrong signal — is why it survived the sutra/276 review, and why sutra/280 fixed the identical hardcoded pair in lessons.rs without noticing this one twelve lines away.</root_cause>
<parameter name="execution_record">language_from_path now resolves the extension through default_registry().adapter_for_extension() and returns String (the registry is owned per call, so a &'static str return was not available). One call-site fix in extract_proposed_imports for the String/&str change.

Behavior-change check performed rather than assumed (the task flagged it): parse_proposed has 8 callers, all in src/guard.rs, feeding proposed-content constraint analysis and is_signature_preserving. Widening the language set puts py/ts/js/c on those paths too. Judged a consistency fix — that is the contract .rs/.dart files already had, and every widened extension belongs to a fully indexed adapter — and documented in the doc comment so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

.pyi confirmed still excluded: pattern-eligible per sutra/275 but not indexed, and PythonAdapter claims only "py". Asserted explicitly in the test.

4 tests: language_from_path across all six adapters plus three negatives; parse_proposed import extraction for Python and TypeScript; end-to-end import_pattern anchor match for greenfield .py and .ts through a real LessonsDb. The last two cover the chain that was actually dead.

Verified: cargo test 1454 passed / 0 failed; no new clippy warnings.
